'''Ostilio Ricci da Fermo''' (1540–1603) was an Italian [[mathematician]].

==Biography==

He was a university professor in [[Florence]] at the [[Accademia delle Arti del Disegno]], founded in 1560 by [[Giorgio Vasari]]. Ricci is also known for being [[Galileo Galilei]]'s teacher.

Ricci was the Court Mathematician to the [[Francesco I de' Medici, Grand Duke of Tuscany|Grand Duke Francesco de' Medici]] in Florence, in 1580, when Galileo attended his lectures in [[Pisa]].

Galileo was enrolled at the [[University of Pisa]], by his father [[Vincenzo Galilei|Vincenzo]], in order to study medicine. Instead, Galilei became more interested in mathematics, after meeting Ostilio Ricci, a former student of [[Niccolò Tartaglia]].<ref name="renamed_from_10_on_20240929152051">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=Ostilio Ricci |url=https://brunelleschi.imss.fi.it/itineraries/biography/OstilioRicci.html |website=brunelleschi.imss.fi.it |publisher=Museum of the History of Science |access-date=23 September 2024}}</ref> Ricci taught Galileo the mathematics of [[Euclid]] and [[Archimedes]], who both deeply influenced Galileo's later work.<ref name="renamed_from_10_on_20240929152051">{{cite web |last= |first= |title=Ostilio Ricci |url=https://brunelleschi.imss.fi.it/itineraries/biography/OstilioRicci.html |website=brunelleschi.imss.fi.it |publisher=Museum of the History of Science |access-date=23 September 2024}}</ref> Ricci considered mathematics not to be a distinct science, but a practical tool for problems in mechanics and engineering. Ostilio Ricci is systematically cited in the various biographies of Galileo Galilei.

He died at age 62, in Florence. Italy. His cause of death remains unknown.
